title: Welcome to FMER
summary: A standalone FM and VA instrument, with a local companion for organizing and protecting your music.
body:
FMER combines six-operator FM and virtual analog synthesis with four mono sequencer tracks, an arpeggiator and shared effects. The companion runs on your own computer. It needs no account or cloud library.

Find your next step

  • Start the companion and edit a sound
  • Organize instruments and projects
  • Record four tracks
  • Back up and restore an FM-1
  • Find a physical control or menu
  • Look up every sound parameter
  • Diagnose a problem

This handbook documents development firmware 735 and Companion 735 r11. Search works offline, including when you open index.htm directly from disk. Print any article with your browser. The qualification and limits page distinguishes available functions from work still pending.

Read Licensing, credits and interoperability to learn how FMER builds on Felucca hardware support and the MSFA FM engine, and which patch formats can move between instruments.

Build and deploy instrument loadout profiles.

title: Your first companion session
summary: Working sound, computer library and unit storage are three separate places.
body:
1. Extract the entire Windows ZIP, then double-click FMER Companion.exe. Keep the extracted folder together. Python, the sound renderer, help and defaults are included. Your default browser opens a local 127.0.0.1 address; no internet connection, account or hosted website is needed.
  2. Open Sound banks. Bank A contains 64 Spectrum instruments: 36 FM and 28 VA. Bank B starts with independent copies; either bank can contain either engine.
  3. Choose a sound and open Editor. Move a slider or choose a musical setting. Exact stored numbers remain visible. Audition renders audio on the computer.
  4. Save an instrument into Library. Give it a descriptive title, collection and tags. This does not write to the unit.
  5. When ready to transfer, connect the unit, read its bank, select a destination and explicitly send the library item. Read the overwrite summary.
  6. Make a unit backup before reorganizing hardware slots. Save a project on the unit when you want its patterns and track assignments available after power-off.

The Editor's working sound can differ from both its PC bank destination and the connected unit. Saving in one place does not silently synchronize the other two. Library titles can be longer than the ten-character instrument names shown by the unit.

On firmware734, GLO first page K1 and SEQ / PLAY MODE K1 choose1V (one synth voice),6V (six voices for one synth) or4T (four mono tracks). On the PRESETS page the SELECT knob also changes playing mode; the PRESETS knob always browses sounds. Voices is locked in4T. The header keeps the current mode visible. Entering or leaving4T releases notes and stops playback. Changing between1V and6V keeps single-instrument sequencing running; browsing sounds and ordinary pages preserve the mode.

Portable application, persistent library

Your music and operation logs live in %LOCALAPPDATA%\FMER\Companion, separate from the executable. Moving the application folder does not move your library. Use Library export and Sound banks backup to transfer music to another PC. The supplied Libraries folder contains a clean catalog of all 64 original defaults. Import it from Library when you want editable catalog copies; existing items are preserved.

Use Quit companion before replacing the application folder. Windows 10/11 x64 is the supported platform. An unsigned download may show a Windows reputation warning; verify the release source and checksum. No administrator installation is required.

Closing and updating

Use Quit companion for immediate shutdown. Closing the last app tab releases the local server after about 45 seconds; a reload or second tab keeps it available. Active transfers continue safely until finished, even if the tab closes. Reopen the app to monitor them. Starting a new version asks an idle older server to quit; a busy older server is left running. You should not need Task Manager.

title: Connect an FM-1
summary: Device operations are explicit and serialized; opening the app does not access the instrument.
body:
The connection badge observes USB MIDI endpoints without taking control of their ports. Unplugging clears the connection and cached unit catalogs; reconnecting requires Check connection. Detected means Windows sees a MIDI endpoint; verified means the unit answered an identity query. Read banks/projects again after reconnecting or writing. Operation results are labeled with their completion time and are historical records.

Check connection in the top-right corner identifies stock firmware, FMER or the updater. A stock device can be connected without supporting FMER library commands. The operation banner shows progress and keeps its result visible; leave power, USB and controls alone until it says Complete.

  1. Power the FM-1 and connect USB directly to the computer.
  2. Close Ableton or release its FMER MIDI ports before companion transfers. Windows MIDI ports may be held exclusively by another application.
  3. Open FM-1 in the companion and read a bank or project catalog. The transport checks the supported FMER identity rather than guessing a device command.
  4. Leave keys and controls untouched during backups or writes. Wait for the operation to finish before disconnecting or starting another transfer.

The companion uses Windows MIDI for FMER 733/734/735 library transfers. A stock FM-1 or a different firmware identity is not automatically a compatible library endpoint. Multiple matching devices are refused rather than selecting an arbitrary unit. macOS and Linux transports remain a later packaging and hardware qualification task.

The operation panel reports progress and retains failed-operation details. A disconnected browser does not cancel a write already running in the local server. Keep the server running and reconnect to inspect the operation.

Standalone Bluetooth MIDI is not available in firmware734. USB MIDI and TRS input remain the qualified transports. A second stock FM-1 cannot yet pair with FMER. The vendor radio-stack integration and clock scheduling need separate hardware qualification.

Managing more than one FM-1

Companion currently manages one connected instrument at a time. If the badge says Multiple FM-1s - connect one, disconnect the other units from this computer and choose Check connection. Identical USB names do not identify a particular instrument. A USB port is not a permanent instrument serial number.

If Windows reports that the MIDI port is already in use, close or disable that instrument's ports in Ableton or other music software. Stop diagnostic capture in another Companion instance before retrying. You do not need to delete your Library or reinstall the application.

title: Instrument loadout profiles
summary: Save ordered 64-instrument profiles and independently populate Bank A and Bank B during installation or later.
body:
A loadout profile stores 64 complete instruments in a fixed order. FM and VA sounds can occupy any slot. Profiles live on this computer until you explicitly apply them to an FM-1.

Build your own collection

  1. Open Instrument loadouts. Choose Spectrum (balanced), Rhythm (drums/bass), Voltage (leads/arp), Atmosphere (pads/weird), or Classic (compiled firmware defaults).
  2. Enter a name and choose Save a copy. Included profiles stay intact.
  3. Select a slot, then Choose instrument. Search included sounds, your Library and PC banks. Listen before replacing the slot.
  4. Use Move earlier, Move later or Move to to reorder the sounds. Undo reverses one committed edit. Name and notes use Save name & notes.
  5. Export profile saves a checksummed .fmer-loadout.json file. Import profile makes a new independent copy. You can keep twelve personal profiles plus the included ones.

Save bank as profile captures a complete PC Bank A or Bank B bank. Fill empty PC slots first. Editing a Library sound later does not change a saved profile; replace the profile slot explicitly to adopt the new version.

Choose Bank A and Bank B independently

Each bank holds 64 instruments. For example, select Spectrum for Bank A and Rhythm for Bank B. You can also choose the same profile for both, or Keep bank unchanged for either one. Review & apply bank choices backs up the unit and writes only the selected banks. It does not flash firmware. Slot numbers00?63 match the unit display.

Choose sounds when installing

  1. Open Firmware and inspect the included FMER package.
  2. Choose a separate profile for Bank A and Bank B, or keep either bank unchanged. On a first install, unchanged banks use the compiled defaults.
  3. Review the named bank replacements and confirm once. Existing supported FMER saves are backed up before installation. Stock firmware does not expose the native backup interface.
  4. Keep USB and power connected while Companion installs, reconnects, backs up initialized banks, writes the instruments and verifies them. This can take several minutes. The progress banner identifies the current phase.

Custom firmware and stock recovery do not receive automatic loadouts. Only the reviewed included FMER release supports this combined workflow.

Your projects and reset actions

Replacing a slot changes the sound of projects using that slot. Projects remain stored, but their instrument references are not remapped. After deployment you can use the unit without Companion. Reset to FMER Default and Reset User Bank still restore the firmware?s compiled Classic collection; your personal profile remains safely on the computer and can be applied again.

If transfer stops

Companion distinguishes completed firmware installation from incomplete bank transfer, retains the list of verified slots, and offers the backup and operation record. There is no automatic rollback or retry. Check the connection and installed banks, then explicitly send the chosen profiles again. A failed bank transfer does not require another firmware installation.

Expressions2 and firmware735

Spectrum A contains all62 favorites from the owner review plus two contrasting bass voices:36 FM and28 VA instruments. B focuses on drums and bass, C on leads and arps, and D on pads, ambience and unusual textures. Each profile holds64 sounds; the combined library contains192 unique original instruments. Classic retains the previous64 defaults. Bank A and Bank B are independent64-slot destinations; either can contain any mix of engines.

PRESETS browses Bank A slots0–63 followed by Bank B slots0–63 in exact loadout order. K1 jumps between those two banks. The header identifies FM or VA. Selecting a patch preserves the playing mode.

Keep existing instruments backs up both banks and materializes inherited sounds affected by a firmware default change. Selected loadouts replace only reviewed destinations. Projects retain slot references, so changing a referenced slot changes its sound. Firmware735 stores native12 records; older versions need a separate storage migration before downgrade.

Browse by sound family

The included Expressions profiles group like instruments together across both engines: bass, leads and arps, keys and plucks, mallets and bells, organs and winds, strings and pads, percussion, then motion and textures. Percussion puts kicks, snares, claps and hats together. Your own saved profiles keep the slot order you choose.

title: Library, collections and Trash
summary: Keep a larger catalog of instruments and projects independently of the unit's slots.
body:
Library holds up to 512 items, subject also to a 10 MiB file limit including Undo history. Each item has a unique identity, instrument/project type, title up to 80 characters, collection, up to 12 distinct tags of 24 characters, notes up to 1,000 characters and a favorite flag. A collection is a label, not a folder path.

Search and type/collection filters narrow the list. Select several items to move them into a collection, duplicate them, export them or send them to Trash. Duplicate creates an independent item. Editing its title does not rename a hardware slot. An instrument's separate ten-character name is stored inside its sound record.

Trash hides items from the normal library. Recover returns them; Empty Catalog Trash permanently removes the currently trashed items from the catalog. Export first if you need a lasting archive. Undo reverses one catalog transaction. It is not a history of all changes and does not reverse device writes.

Import merges a catalog file using new item identities. Restore Local Catalog replaces the local catalog after explicit confirmation; it leaves PC banks and the FM-1 alone. Catalog checksums detect accidental alteration. Writes use a lock, revision check and atomic replacement, retaining the previous file and operation journal.

Prepare a live set

  1. Select the relevant instruments and projects.
  2. Move them to a collection named after the set.
  3. Add song/order tags and mark favorites.
  4. Export the selection as a portable catalog file.
  5. Back up the unit before assigning these sounds to hardware slots; projects reference slot numbers.

Exchange FM sounds with DX7-compatible editors

  1. In Felucca's FM6 editor, export the desired sound as standard DX7 .syx, or use an existing DX7 single voice or32-voice bank you have permission to use.
  2. In FMER Companion Library, choose Import DX7 FM and select the .syx file. The importer validates framing, checksum and parameter ranges before changing the local catalog.
  3. Review the decoded sounds, then import. A single voice adds one instrument; a bank adds32. Import is one local transaction and can be undone. No unit is written automatically.
  4. Open an imported instrument in Editor to audition and adjust it. Imported voices start with dry FMER effects. Use Prepare unit transfer when you deliberately want to write a hardware slot.
  5. To send voices back, select exactly one or32 FM instrument items and choose Export DX7 FM. Exporting creates a local .syx download. VA instruments and projects are refused.

Supported files are one163-byte single-voice message or one4104-byte32-voice bank. Export preserves the six-operator FM parameters and ten-character name; FMER effects, VA controls, patterns, songs and globals are outside DX7 SysEx. Felucca native JSON/project/other engines are different formats and are not imported. A shared patch does not guarantee identical sound across different synth implementations.

Rename and deploy a set

  1. Select an item. Set Instrument name on unit (1-10 printable ASCII characters) and choose Save name & details. The longer Library title is for this computer only.
  2. Select the sounds to deploy and choose Send selected to unit. Choose each destination in the review table, or use Place in Bank B/Bank A, Starting slot and Place consecutively to position an instrument set in one action. The start selector prevents crossing the bank boundary. Project bundles retain individual reference-based destinations.
  3. Review names and slots, then confirm. Companion backs up the complete unit before writing and verifies each slot. On success it downloads that backup and restores the working state with playback stopped.

Import file also accepts an FMER PC sound-bank JSON file: it merges populated sounds into the Library as independent copies, with one Undo. It does not replace the PC banks or write the unit. Get updates & sound packs opens GitHub in your browser. Download the original default catalog separately or import it from the portable ZIP's Libraries folder.

Included OEM patches and community FM voice capture are available from Library / Included & community sounds.

title: Sound banks and instrument slots
summary: Bank A and Bank B are both editable. Reset actions have deliberately separate scopes.
body:
There are 64 Bank A and 64 Bank B instruments. The PC bank file and hardware banks are independent. In the PC file Bank A is 0–63 and Bank B is 64–127; the device protocol uses Bank B 0–63 and Bank A 64–127. The app translates these positions and labels the destinations.

Rename changes the native ten-character ASCII instrument name. Copy duplicates into a chosen destination; review an occupied destination before replacing it. PC Move requires a populated Bank B source and an empty destination. Swap exchanges two entries. Delete is available for PC Bank B entries; Bank A must remain populated. PC bank Undo reverses one PC transaction.

  • Reset to FMER Default: restore the 64 Bank A instruments to the supplied profile.
  • Reset User Bank: restore independent copies of the 64 FMER defaults to Bank B.
  • Clear User Bank: clear Bank B only, after explicit confirmation.

Choose PC or unit actions carefully: resetting a PC bank does not reset hardware. Hardware rename, copy and swap use native records and verification. A swap is two writes, not an atomic transaction. Existing projects keep their numeric references; swapping instruments changes what those projects will play. Current firmware has no individual hardware-slot delete operation, so the app does not simulate one by uploading an arbitrary blank patch.

The 64 original FMER default instruments are GPL-3.0-only. Their editable recipes and license are included with the companion. Imported sounds keep their original rights; see licensing and credits.

Deploy your PC bank

Choose Send sound to unit for one entry or Send this bank to unit for all populated slots in the displayed bank. The review defaults to the corresponding Bank B or Bank A destinations and lets you change them. Confirm only after checking every slot. Empty PC slots leave the unit unchanged. The complete unit is backed up before the first write; each write is verified and working state is restored with playback stopped. Projects keep their slot references, so rearranging sounds can affect existing arrangements. Local Undo does not undo hardware writes.

title: Edit and audition
summary: Visual controls retain the exact underlying values and keep working changes explicit.
body:
The Editor provides synth, envelope/modulation, effects and sequencing controls appropriate to the active engine. Frequency sliders use logarithmic scaling so low-frequency edits remain useful; the number is still the real Hz value. Named choices show their canonical values. Optional numeric entry supports precise settings. One slider gesture is one Undo action.

The bank destination is shown beside the loaded sound. Save there updates that PC bank entry. Save to Library captures a separate instrument or project item. Revert restores the editor's saved state. Opening another item asks before discarding unsaved changes.

Audition renders through the shared host synthesizer and provides playable audio with measured output information. Choose a note, chord, sequence or arp phrase where offered. A selected-pattern audition is not a complete four-track hardware performance qualification. Host rendering does not prove hardware timing or USB reliability.

FX profiles contain effect settings. Importing one preserves the synth and pattern data and can be undone. They are parameter presets, not downloadable executable effect plugins.

Saving refreshes the current PC banks without discarding your draft. If the destination changed in another tab or in PC sound banks, review its current name before replacing it; Cancel keeps both versions. If another change occurs during saving, nothing is overwritten and your edits remain available. Press Save again to review and retry. Opening PC sound banks refreshes saved names and slots.

title: FM synthesis and algorithms
summary: Six operators shape both loudness and changing harmonic content.
body:
An operator is an oscillator with its own envelope. A carrier reaches the output; a modulator changes another operator's phase and therefore its spectrum. Increasing a carrier level mainly changes loudness. Increasing a modulator level can dramatically brighten or roughen the tone. Output level is logarithmic, not a linear percentage.

The algorithm chooses the routing among six operators. The diagram shows the actual operator connections and carriers. Unsupported feedback routing is identified rather than silently advertised as working. Algorithm is saved per instrument; editing the active sound does not rewrite the other bank entries. The display uses human-friendly algorithms 1–32 while the canonical value is 0–31.

FM EDIT selects an operator with SELECT on its first six pages. TUNE holds output level, coarse/fine frequency and detune. SENSITIVITY holds amplitude/velocity sensitivity, ratio/fixed mode and rate scaling. KEY SCALE and CURVE change level across the keyboard. OP RATES and OP LEVELS expose all four envelope stages. PITCH RATES and PITCH LEVELS affect the whole FM voice.

Ratio mode follows the played note; coarse zero is a half ratio. Fixed mode produces a frequency independent of keyboard pitch. Detune is centered at raw 7. Four envelope rates control speeds toward four levels; rate 99 is fastest. Level 3 is held until release, then rate 4 approaches level 4. A silent release normally uses level 4 equal to zero.

Build a brassy attack

  1. Choose a routing with a modulator feeding a carrier.
  2. Raise that modulator's output while playing a comfortable middle register.
  3. Give its first envelope level a strong peak, then reduce the held level. This makes the attack brighter than the sustain.
  4. Increase velocity sensitivity for dynamic attacks; adjust the carrier separately for audible level.
  5. Compare soft and hard notes, low and high registers, then save the instrument.

FM ENV is a quick carrier-envelope view. Use EDIT for independent operator timbre envelopes. FMER is not certified as an exact DX7 emulator; the limitations remain relevant when comparing classic patches.

title: VA synthesis and mono glide
summary: Oscillator, voice filter and envelope form the VA instrument; glide is available for mono playing.
body:
The VA engine offers sine, saw, square and triangle waveforms, a voice low-pass filter, ADSR and modulation. The voice filter belongs to the synthesizer; the shared FX filter is a separate stage. Attack, decay and release are stored in milliseconds. Sustain is a held level.

VA EDIT holds waveform, cutoff and resonance. ENV holds attack, decay, sustain and release. LFO holds rate and pitch depth, plus its enable gate; disabling modulation retains its settings for later use.

GLO / VOICE controls mono/poly capacity. GLO / MONO GLIDE selects glide mode, time and contour. Glide applies to a one-voice instrument. Off changes pitch immediately; always glides between notes; legato glides while another note is held. Linear, eased and exponential contours change the transition shape. Last-held-note priority returns toward a still-held earlier key when the newer key is released.

Make a bass

  1. Choose saw or square and a low octave.
  2. Use a short attack, moderate decay and lower sustain.
  3. Lower the voice cutoff and add resonance gradually.
  4. Set one voice, legato glide and a short transition time.
  5. Play overlapping notes and then separated notes to hear the difference.

Four-track sequencing budgets one mono voice per track. It does not provide four independent four-voice instruments.

title: Filter, reverb, delay and other effects
summary: Three FX pages control a shared effects chain, with activity feedback.
body:
FX page 1 places cutoff, resonance, reverb return and delay return on K1–K4. ALGORITHM selects low-pass, high-pass or band-pass filtering. Low-pass reduces highs, high-pass reduces lows and band-pass emphasizes a band. Resonance emphasizes the selected region; changes can substantially alter level and timbre.

FX page 2 holds chorus, phaser, distortion and the program LFO on/off gate. FX page 3 exposes delay time, delay feedback, reverb size and reverb model. On FX page 2, turn the Chorus or Phaser amount to focus it, then turn ALGORITHM to choose one of four named modulation recipes. The amount slider controls the contribution. On page 3, ALGORITHM selects FREE MS or a synchronized delay division. See the panel map for exact control roles.

Room and Plate are different reverb structures. Size changes the decay character. Clean and Warm delay offer different feedback coloration. Delay time spans 20–1,000 ms and feedback 0–85. Raising a return adds the effect while preserving the dry instrument rather than replacing it with a quiet wet signal. Chorus thickens, phaser moves spectral notches and distortion adds harmonics.

The LFO gate also works from the LFO menu. It enables the currently stored modulation settings without erasing them. Small activity indicators show effect contributions; they are not precision loudness meters. The oscilloscope shows the combined output.

PERFORM / FX lets each track feed the shared chain or bypass it. It does not allocate a separate reverb and delay to every track. Existing tails may continue after a send is disabled. The final digital output clamp contains out-of-range samples but cannot guarantee safe acoustic volume in an external amplification system.

Delay sync and space characters /722

On FX page3, turn ALGORITHM to select FREE MS0 or note divisions1..7. K1 edits milliseconds in FREE or the division in sync. The saved free time survives mode changes. The footer shows actual delay time; MAX means the one-second buffer cannot fit the requested slow division. Tempo follows internal BPM or received MIDI clock. Reverb choices are Room0, Plate1, Hall2 and Cloud3. Hall is darker and longer; Cloud has a longer, more modulated tail. The filter has a stronger resonant peak, especially in band pass. Reverb return is stronger while the dry path is retained.

In four-track mode ARP and FX show the track number and M (muted, including another track solo), S (solo), and FX1/FX0. Mixer routing stays active when you change pages. Return to SEQ/PERFORM to change those flags; navigation never clears a performance mix.

HOME and FX page1 share the same knob order: cutoff, FX resonance, reverb, delay. HP fills right, LP left, BP around cutoff. FM feedback is in EDIT / CURVE on knob2. Named choices omit internal enum indices; actual musical numbers retain units.

Reorder the signal chain

Press FX to reach SIGNAL CHAIN, the fourth page. K1 or ALGORITHM selects a stage; K2 moves it earlier or later; K3 restores the original order. The complete list reads from input at the top to output at the bottom. The original order is Filter, Reverb, Delay, Distortion, Chorus, Phaser. Existing effect-control pages stay in place. The companion Editor FX tab offers Earlier and Later buttons with Undo.

Order is saved with instruments, projects and FX profiles. Browsing sounds keeps the current FX, including their order; an explicit sound load restores the saved chain. All four tracks use the same chain, with independent FX bypass. The VA voice filter acts before this bus. LFO is modulation, not a seventh serial effect. Moving a stage can change loudness and coloration; tails are retained while routing changes.

Your default signal chain

FX page4 shows the actual six-stage order. K1 or ALGORITHM selects an effect; K2 moves it; K3 resets to your saved default. Hold SEL and press FX to save the current chain as your personal default. This stops playback for a guarded onboard settings write. Wait for Bank A SAVED. It survives power-off and does not rewrite sound banks or projects.

GLO / RESET-CLEAR / ORIGINAL FX ROUTE, then SEL twice, restores and applies Filter → Reverb → Delay → Distortion → Chorus → Phaser as the default. Other resets leave your routing default alone. Explicit sound/project loads retain their own saved chain; the personal default is the reset target and fresh-state boot fallback, not an override of saved music. Ordinary preset browsing continues to preserve live FX. A complete unit backup includes the personal default; a sound/project export does not.

Chorus and phaser character

On FX page 2, turn the Chorus or Phaser knob to select that effect, then turn ALGORITHM through its four characters. Chorus: Dream, Wide, Shimmer, Rush. Phaser: Drift, Sweep, Pulse, Storm. The amount slider remains independent and reaches a 50/50 dry/wet blend at full intensity; retaining the dry sound produces the strongest chorus blend or phaser notches. The chosen character saves with the project. The companion has matching character selectors and includes them in exported FX profiles.

Chorus and phaser recipes

Each effect has four recipes ranging from slower movement to faster or stronger modulation. Their selections are saved with the sound and version 4 FX profile. Depth remains independently adjustable. Recipes do not allocate extra effects or change the six-stage chain.

Chorus recipes: DREAM, WIDE, SHIMMER, RUSH. Phaser recipes: DRIFT, SWEEP, PULSE, STORM. Turn the corresponding amount first, then turn ALGORITHM. Their names describe increasing speed and movement, not additional independent effects.

title: Envelopes, LFOs and control scaling
summary: Understand time-based sound changes and the difference between FM and VA envelopes.
body:
An envelope changes a value in response to a note. VA uses attack, decay, sustain and release. FM uses four rates and four destination levels per operator, plus a global pitch envelope. The FM ENV shortcut affects carriers, while EDIT exposes each operator independently. Modulators with changing envelopes create evolving brightness even when output loudness stays steady.

An LFO is a repeating low-frequency modulation source. FM provides waveform, rate, pitch depth, amplitude depth, delay, sensitivity and sync controls. VA provides its implemented pitch modulation controls. The enable gate is shared with the FX toggle. Stored settings remain when modulation is off.

On the unit, the four parameter knobs cover their full usable range. Holding SEL gives a finer edit around the current value; frequency and time controls use appropriate nonlinear scaling. Always check the displayed canonical value. SELECT is the rotary selector; SEL is the separate button used for fine adjustment or page-specific confirmation.

Repeated ARP or LFO button presses can toggle their active state. Use SELECT for their pages instead of assuming every family button only advances a page. The panel map documents the exceptions.

title: Arpeggiator
summary: Turn held or latched notes into a rhythmic phrase.
body:
Press ARP to enter the arpeggiator. Enable it, play several notes and set the type. Latch retains the note set after keys are released. Octaves extends the pitch span. Triplets changes the subdivision relationship. The second page holds division, tempo, gate and swing so those timing settings keep consistent positions.

The ten stored type codes are 0 Up, 1 Down, 2 Exclusive, 3 Played, 4 Inclusive, 5 Random, 6 Repeat, 7 Down exclusive, 8 Down inclusive and 9 Outside-in. Exclusive pendulum traversal avoids repeating the end notes at reversal; inclusive repeats them. Played follows input order. Random chooses from the available notes. Gate changes the sounding portion of each step and swing alternates timing.

  1. Hold a triad and choose Up.
  2. Set two octaves and a short gate.
  3. Enable latch and release the keys.
  4. Compare Exclusive and Inclusive to hear the turnaround difference.
  5. For synchronization, choose the external clock source and send transport Start from the master.

Arp and sequencer share bounded voice and transport resources. A stopped external clock or absent note set can legitimately produce silence. MIDI output routing determines whether generated arp notes are sent to another instrument.

Capture the generated phrase

Choose the target track and pattern, enable the arp, then press REC on the ARP page. Four quiet quarter-note clicks lead into a shared downbeat; held or latched notes generate the recorded phrase. Existing Overdub/Replace applies; Step mode is changed to Overdub for this timed capture. REC again finishes capture while leaving the arp enabled. The pattern is mono and quantized to sixteenths: faster divisions, swing and Repeat chords are reduced to the last onset in each cell, not a lossless MIDI recording. Save the project to retain the take.

Strum (Type10) makes one ascending pass through the held chord. Rate sets spacing, Gate sets length, and a fresh key rearms the pass. Record from ARP to capture the generated notes.

title: Four-track recording and patterns
summary: Sixteen shared patterns, up to 64 steps each, with one instrument per mono track.
body:
The pattern pool is 16 patterns total, shared by four tracks. Each pattern contains up to 64 steps with pitch, velocity and gate. Rest is stored as 128 and Tie as 129; playable MIDI notes are 0–127. A tie extends an earlier note rather than making a new attack. Reducing a pattern's visible length retains its hidden steps for later expansion.

Each track chooses a saved instrument reference and a pattern, with independent level, mute, solo and FX routing. Pattern changes queue independently at that track's pattern boundary. Chains select a cyclic sequence of patterns. The separate SONG page adds four independent arrangement lanes with per-entry repeats and transposition. See Song mode.

RECORD offers Step, Overdub and Replace (stored 0, 1 and 2). Step entry writes deliberate events. Timed Overdub preserves existing events where you do not play. Replace records a new pass in place of the prior events. The four-beat count-in silences playback and starts all tracks together on the downbeat, aligning the recording pass. REC ends recording while allowing playback to continue; PLAY/STOP stops transport.

Record a small arrangement

  1. Save kick, snare, bass and lead sounds to known slots.
  2. Assign one to each track and choose four distinct patterns.
  3. Set tempo and pattern lengths before recording.
  4. Select the first track, choose timed Overdub, then press REC and wait through the count-in.
  5. Record the part; end recording and repeat for the other tracks.
  6. Use PERFORM to balance levels, mute and queue patterns.
  7. Save a project so the pattern pool, assignments and mix can be recalled.

Step/pattern numbers are displayed in context; native pattern references are zero-based 0–15. An external clock master must send the expected clock and transport events when the unit is waiting for it.

Performance navigation

Hold HOME and press SEQ to open MIXER in four-track mode. ALGORITHM or SELECT cycles Patch, Pattern, Run, Volume, Mute, Solo, FX. Each of the four knobs belongs to its corresponding track. Transport uses a white solid triangle/square for current play/stop; pending launch/retrigger blinks pink. Hold SEL and tap PLAY for the selected track to restart at the next bar; double-tap PLAY while holding SEL queues all four.

Single-instrument playback

In SINGLE mode, PLAY runs one mono pattern lane through your current instrument. Pattern queues, chains and Song lane 1 are available. Remaining voices can play live keys or an arp alongside the pattern. With glide enabled there is only one total voice, so simultaneous parts compete for it. Browsing SEQ pages never changes mode. Choose the mode explicitly on SEQ → MODE, GLO → VOICE, or with a documented shortcut.

Get to the right sequencer page

Press SEQ from another section to land on MIXER in4T or the single-lane SONG in1V/6V. Hold SEQ for0.8 seconds to return there from any sequencer page. Repeated taps follow MIXER (4T only), SONG, PATTERNS, STEP EDIT, NOTE EDIT, COPY/EDIT, RECORD, CHAIN and PLAY MODE. Where SELECT navigates pages, turn backward to reverse this order; SONG keeps SELECT for entry selection and MIXER keeps it for layers. Merely browsing pages never switches playing mode. Hold HOME then press SEQ for the explicit four-track mixer shortcut.

title: Hand-edit notes, rests and sections
summary: Edit timing and duration without recording another pass.
body:
SEQ / STEP EDIT uses K1 for the step cursor, K2 for pitch, K3 for velocity and K4 for gate. SEQ / NOTE EDIT uses cursor, pitch, note length and gate. Select a note and turn ALGORITHM to move the whole event earlier or later. A move that collides with another event is refused rather than silently deleting that event.

SEL deletes the selected note. With SEL held, pitch changes can enter a rest or tie. Rest leaves silence at that step; Tie continues an earlier note. Length editing extends a note through tie steps. The gate is the fraction of a step spent sounding, not the number of tied steps.

SEQ / COPY/EDIT uses K1 for range start, K2 for count, K3 for destination and K4 for the action. Press SEL to apply Copy, Paste, Cut, Clear or guarded Undo. The clipboard is temporary, not a saved project library. Manual destructive edits are blocked during active recording. Undo only applies when its source state is still valid.

Write a phrase

  1. Choose an empty pattern and set its length.
  2. At step 1 enter a pitch and velocity.
  3. Use NOTE EDIT to hold it for four steps.
  4. Leave the next step as a rest, then enter the next note.
  5. Copy a short range to a later destination and alter its pitch.
  6. Play the phrase, move any early/late event, then save the project.

title: The performance mixer
summary: Four fixed track columns keep live controls in consistent positions.
body:
SEQ / PERFORM is a vertical mixer. K1–K4 always address tracks 1–4. ALGORITHM, SELECT or SEL selects the layer: Patch, Pattern, Run, Volume, Mute, Solo, FX. The screen shows the active layer and each track's state.

  • Level: changes the local track level, not a transmitted MIDI CC7.
  • Pattern: queues a change at that track's boundary.
  • Sound: chooses a saved instrument slot; the project retains a reference to it.
  • Mute: silences that track while its timeline continues.
  • Solo: allows selected solo tracks through together; mute still wins for a muted track.
  • FX: enables or bypasses the shared effect path for that track.

D/U identify Bank A/Bank B sound references; P identifies patterns. M, S and F mark mute, solo and FX state. Visit FX with its dedicated button and return to SEQ without stopping playback. Entering or leaving4T stops playback; switching between1V and6V or viewing pages does not.

All four local tracks are mono. A split MIDI output routes them onto consecutive channels for external recording, while merged output places generated notes together. Neither mode creates four independent USB audio streams.

Launch and stop at a bar

RUN follows Pattern and precedes Volume in the mixer layer order. Turn a track knob left to stop that cursor immediately, releasing its current note. Turn right to launch its queued pattern (or restart its current pattern) at the next global16-step downbeat. Hold SEL and tap PLAY to queue the last touched track; hold SEL and double-tap PLAY within300ms to queue all four. The master clock keeps its phase. Recording/count-in refuses launch changes. Ordinary pattern queues still wait for their own pattern boundary. A full Stop/Start starts all tracks again.

Mixer feel

LEVEL moves two percentage points per slow detent and accelerates to four or six during a continuous faster turn. Hold SEL for exactly one percentage point per detent. Changing direction, knob or fine mode resets acceleration. Other mixer layers keep their existing discrete behavior.

Meaningful lights

The selected page is bright. Enabled FX and LFO are dim when on another page. SAVE is dim for an edited working sound, blinks during a storage operation, briefly lights after verified completion and pulses more slowly on failure. The SAVE page itself stays bright as navigation feedback. REC pulses with the count-in clicks and stays bright during capture. ARP pulses with generated gates even on its own page; held chord keys remain dim while sounding generated pitches brighten. Short button taps receive a brief acknowledgement. Key lights still represent their actual octave and note ownership; no unrelated decorative animation is added.

Live keys while stopped

With the sequencer stopped and no recording armed, physical keys and arps audition the selected instrument through saved mute/solo settings. Track level, FX routing and Local Off still apply. Starting playback or recording restores mixer mute/solo control. Audition does not change or save your mix. Incoming external MIDI continues to follow mixer mutes.

Choose1V,6V or4T directly

SEQ / PLAY MODE K1 and GLO / VOICE/TEMPO K1 both offer1V,6V and4T. On PRESETS, SELECT chooses the same playing mode while PRESETS continues to browse sounds. Choose6V for four-note synth playing,1V for a mono instrument or4T for four independent mono tracks. Choosing1V enables Legato glide unless another glide mode is already selected;6V and4T turn glide off. The mode wheel stops at either end rather than wrapping around. Entering or leaving4T stops playback and releases notes while preserving patterns, assignments and mix. Switching between1V and6V keeps single-instrument sequencing running. Voices stays locked in4T. ALGORITHM still selects the track on PLAY MODE. PLAY MODE K2 selects glide Off/Legato/Always in single-instrument modes, K3 sets glide time and K4 its contour. Glide selects one voice; turning it off restores the previous single-instrument voice budget.

Playing-mode continuity

PRESETS changes your sound without changing SINGLE/4TRK or your single-instrument glide/polyphony setting. Loading a full project deliberately restores its playing mode. In either mode, press HOME again for fullscreen waveforms; four-track fullscreen shows four part traces above the master mix.

Finding controls in darkness

Action buttons and piano keys have a faint locating glow. Bright signals current navigation, a press, transport or an active note. Octave direction is shown by OCT−/OCT+: one octave is dim, two half brightness, three full brightness; a press briefly brightens the button. At zero both remain at locating brightness. The numeric octave value remains the exact reference.

In Companion, a two- or three-voice limit is shown as 2V or 3V Custom voice limit, rather than 6V. This can come from an imported sound or the advanced Voices slider. Choose 6V explicitly to restore the full four-voice budget.

Octave lights

OCT- and OCT+ show the direction of keyboard transpose. Zero uses the faint ready glow. One octave uses half brightness, two use three-quarter brightness, and three use full brightness. Pressing either button briefly lights it fully; the steady brightness after release shows the octave distance.

title: Save and recall projects
summary: A project stores arrangement state and references to sounds, not four immutable sound copies.
body:
The unit has 16 project destinations, separate from its 128 instrument slots. Projects contain the working sound/state, 16 patterns, track assignments, chain and mixer settings. Each track's sound reference points to an instrument slot. Replacing that slot later can change a recalled project.

  1. Save edited instruments first.
  2. Assign their slots to the tracks.
  3. Press SAVE and select Project with K4; select the destination with K1.
  4. Choose Save or Load with K3 and confirm with SEL.

In the companion, project titles are catalog metadata. Current firmware does not expose independent on-device project-name fields. A project captured from the PC Editor can include snapshots of referenced sounds found in the PC banks. These are explicitly PC snapshots, not proof of what currently occupies the unit. A basic device project pull contains the native project record.

Sending a project record does not silently overwrite all its referenced instruments. Review or transfer those sounds separately to their expected slots. A complete unit backup is the reliable way to preserve the actual sound and project banks together. Standard DX7 banks, native FMER records, companion catalogs, PC bank files and unit backups are different formats and should not be renamed to impersonate one another.

Use Extract embedded sounds in project details to create independently editable Library instruments from the included snapshots. Their notes retain the original slot references for deliberate deployment.

733 save compatibility

733 uses Native11 records of the same 4,000-byte size. Existing saves migrate without a bank reset. Chorus/phaser character now survives save/recall. Older firmware and tools cannot import Native11 files; keep your original backups if you need to return to an older version.

Deploy a project bundle

Send project with sounds appears when Library project details contain embedded instruments. It opens one review containing the project and those sound destinations. Instruments are written before the project, after a complete destination backup. Choose the same instrument slots referenced by the project; this action does not rewrite references. Prepare unit transfer sends only the project record. A failed multi-slot operation can leave earlier writes completed; the operation record identifies them and retains the full pre-transfer backup.

title: MIDI, clocks and recording to a DAW
summary: Fixed CC map, all198 parameter IDs, MIDI Learn limitations, exact SysEx examples, patch selection and DAW workflows.
body:
Are parameter IDs MIDI CC numbers?

No. Firmware 735 has 198 fixed canonical parameter IDs (0 through 197). These are FMER addresses used by its panel, companion and exact USB SysEx protocol. They are not automatically CCs or NRPNs. For example, shared filter cutoff is parameter 162, controlled by CC74 in SINGLE mode; shared filter resonance is parameter 146 and has no fixed CC. CC71 controls a different parameter: VA voice resonance (163).

The complete parameter table gives each ID, legal range, meaning, menu location and any CC shortcut. IDs0 through144 retain the FM voice compatibility order: OP6 first, OP1 last. The current IDs145 through159 are assigned controls, not unused slots; older protocol notes describing them as reserved do not apply to734. Treat this as a versioned interface: new firmware may extend capabilities or ranges, so check its reference rather than assuming an older map is complete.

Is there a MIDI Learn mode?

No built-in MIDI Learn or saved custom CC assignments exist in734, either on the instrument or in the companion. The fixed CC numbers below cannot be reassigned in FMER. NRPN/RPN control is not implemented. A controller's own editor can assign its knobs to FMER's fixed CCs. A DAW or external MIDI processor may translate other controls into those CCs or supported USB SysEx; that mapping lives in the external software, not in FMER.

Use an external controller to play and automate FMER

  1. For a computer, choose PC/NORMAL on GLO / USB LINK, connect USB and enable FMER as a MIDI output destination in your software. A class-compliant controller needs a suitable host; a cable alone does not make every controller a USB host. TRS supports musical MIDI input, not output. The companion's exact editor protocol is USB-only.
  2. Set GLO / MIDI INPUT to Omni or the channel your controller sends. In4TRK mode, incoming channels1,2,3,4 address tracks1,2,3,4; use Omni to control all four. The outgoing KEY CH setting does not change those incoming track assignments.
  3. Assign absolute knobs with values0 through127: CC74 cutoff, CC71 VA resonance, CC73 attack, CC72 release, CC12 delay, CC91 reverb, CC93 chorus and CC95 phaser. Relative encoder formats are not decoded as increments; use the controller's absolute mode or an external translator.
  4. Test with a held note, then a newly played note. Some instrument edits take effect through voice configuration/new notes; a changed number does not guarantee a sustained voice will morph. Shared effects affect the common bus.
  5. Record these CC messages into a MIDI clip for automation and route playback back to FMER. SEND KNOBS is not needed for incoming control. Save the instrument or project explicitly if you want the edited state after power-off; sending a CC does not write a preset bank.

CC values are7-bit absolute values, not the displayed engineering units. For shared FX amount,0 means0%,64 means50%,127 means100%. Single-mode attack/release use floor(value x10000/127) milliseconds. Cutoff is logarithmic: CC74=0 means20Hz and127 means20000Hz in SINGLE, or18000Hz for the addressed VA part in4TRK. Do not send the number1000 as a CC value to request1000Hz: use SysEx for exact Hz. CC7/channel volume and CC11/expression are performance controls, not the stored mixer-fader parameter157.

Use FMER knobs to control a DAW

  1. On GLO / MIDI CLOCK, turn SEND KNOBS on. Set the base output channel on GLO / MIDI OUTPUT and press SEL to retain the MIDI setup.
  2. In your DAW, enable its MIDI mapping/remote input for FMER. Activate the DAW's Learn function, choose a software control and move an FMER control that changes one of the eight mapped parameters above. Exit Learn and test. This is the DAW's Learn feature; FMER is sending its fixed CC.
  3. In4TRK, the four tone CCs use the selected track's split/merged output channel. The four shared FX amount CCs use the base channel. Layer changes on the mixer do not create new CC mappings.
  4. Avoid an unintended return route to FMER. Incoming CCs are not echoed, but an external feedback loop or duplicated note routing can still make the setup confusing.

Moving an FM operator, algorithm, mixer fader, mute, solo, tempo or another unmapped control does not emit a corresponding automatic CC. Manual preset browsing does not emit Bank Select/Program Change. A generic DAW Learn button cannot discover an ID for a control that sends no MIDI message.

GLO / MIDI INPUT selects Omni or an input channel. GLO / MIDI OUTPUT uses K1 for route (0 Off, 1 Keys, 2 Seq/Arp, 3 Auto), K2 for the base channel, K3 for local sound and K4 for split/merged routing (0 Split, 1 Merged). Stored channel 0 is musical channel 1. Split sends sequencer tracks on base channel plus track offset (wrapping after channel16); merged uses one channel.

GLO / MIDI CLOCK selects source (0 Internal, 1 USB, 2 TRS input), clock output, transport receive and parameter CC send. SEL persists MIDI settings. Supported parameter CC output is scoped to the implemented mappings, including 71–74; it is not an automatic mapping of every control. Incoming pitch bend, sustain and note ownership are handled by the musical engine; stop/panic releases owned notes.

Record four MIDI parts in Ableton

  1. Set output to Seq/Arp or Auto, base channel 1 and Split.
  2. Create four DAW MIDI tracks listening to FMER channels 1, 2, 3 and 4.
  3. Choose one clock master. For an external master, enable FMER transport receive and select the correct clock source.
  4. Arm the DAW tracks and send Start. Check each part before a long take.
  5. For one combined MIDI recording, use Merged or listen to all channels on one DAW track.

Local sound can be disabled when FMER is controlling an external synthesizer. Avoid routing outgoing MIDI straight back to the unit unless the DAW routing is intentional. A clock-loss guard prevents a missing external clock from leaving an uncontrolled transport.

USB audio is the combined mono master duplicated into the advertised stereo capture stream. Four separate audio stems are not available. Record parts separately if you need isolated audio. Long USB recording reliability still has an open underrun issue; verify a take before relying on it. The qualified TRS port is input-only.

GLO page 4: MIDI OUTPUT

  • K1 SEND: Off (0), physical Keys (1), generated ARP/SEQ notes (2), or Auto (3), which selects played keys or generated notes according to the current mode. Incoming MIDI is not echoed.
  • K2 KEY CH: the base output channel, displayed 1 through 16 (stored 0 through 15).
  • K3 HEAR FMER: On (1) enables the local instrument; Off (0) lets the unit control another instrument silently.
  • K4 CH MODE: Split (0) sends four sequencer tracks on base channel plus offsets0,1,2,3 (base1 gives channels1 through 4); Merged (1) sends them on the selected base channel.

GLO page 5: MIDI CLOCK

  • K1 TEMPO: Own BPM (0), USB In (1), or TRS In (2).
  • K2 SEND CLOCK: sends FMER clock/transport to USB MIDI when enabled.
  • K3 MIDI START: follow incoming Start/Stop when on; ignore transport messages when off. Clock source is chosen independently.
  • K4 SEND KNOBS: sends the supported tone controls as MIDI CC when on.

These settings apply globally. Changes take effect immediately; SEL saves them for the next power-on. GLO advances pages and HOME returns. The page explains the active routing or clock choice above the four controls.

Switch patches from a DAW or controller

Send CC0 (Bank MSB), CC32=0 (Bank LSB), then Program Change on the intended channel. Bank0 selects the64 Bank A sounds; Bank1 selects Bank B. Program values are0 through 63; software displaying1 through 128 calls these programs1 through 64. Existing Program Change with no Bank Select still selects Bank A after boot. Bank selection is remembered independently for every receive channel and USB/TRS source until reboot or another Bank Select.

Bank A program IDs are stable: FM slots0 through 7 use programs0 through 7; FM slots8 through 31 use programs16 through 39. VA slots0 through 7 use programs8 through 15; VA slots8 through 31 use programs40 through 63. Bank B programs0 through 63 map directly to Bank B slots0 through 63. Names and engine can change when you overwrite a slot.

In single-instrument mode, the accepted channel selects the live instrument. In four-track mode, channels1 through 4 select tracks1 through 4, including tracks not currently selected on screen. Set input to Omni for all four. Unsupported banks, nonzero LSB, programs64 through 127 and empty User slots leave the instrument unchanged. Patch selection reads the cached bank; it does not write flash, load a project, replace the live shared FX or restart the sequence. It can retrigger/release the affected voice; seamless held-note morphing is not promised.

Example: on channel3, send B2 00 01, B2 20 00, C2 05 (hex) to select Bank B slot5 on track3. To return to Bank A, send bank MSB0, LSB0 and the desired program. Incoming Program Change is not echoed; manual patch browsing does not transmit Program Change in734.

Implemented MIDI control map

MessageInput behaviorOutput
Notes / velocity / pitch bendChannel-filtered synth control; bend is14-bitKeys and generated notes per SEND; no incoming echo or panel bend output
CC1 /7 /11 /64Mod wheel / channel volume / expression / sustainNot automatically emitted
CC71VA voice resonance0 through 95%; not the shared FX filter resonanceSEND KNOBS
CC72 /73Voice release / attack,0 through 10000msSEND KNOBS
CC74Single: shared cutoff20 through 20000Hz; four-track: addressed VA voice cutoff20 through 18000Hz; logarithmicSEND KNOBS; split track controls on base channel plus selected track offset
CC12 /91 /93 /95Shared delay / reverb / chorus / phaser amount0 through 100%; affects the shared bus, not individual track sendsSEND KNOBS, base channel
CC120 /121 /123All Sound Off / reset supported performance controllers / All Notes Off; sustain semantics applyRecovery termination when required; not a generic panel mapping
Clock / Start / Continue / Stop / SPPChosen USB or TRS clock source; transport receive must be enabled for transport and song positionInternal clock and Start/Continue/Stop when SEND CLOCK is on; SPP output absent
FMER SysExAll198 canonical parameters with exact integer ranges; separate native/project/FX-routing and guarded storage operationsRequested state/status replies; not generic CC automation

CC amount input uses floor(value x100/127); the exact resulting percentage appears on FMER. 7-bit CC cannot provide exact precision across every frequency/time value; use companion SysEx for that. CC receive does not echo CC output. Poly/channel pressure, NRPN/RPN, MIDI2, BLE and automatic Program Change output are not implemented. Standard Bank Select and effect control naming follow the MIDI Association table; CC12 is FMER's documented delay-amount assignment.

Advanced: edit any canonical parameter by USB SysEx

Use the companion for ordinary editing and verified transfers. Custom controllers/scripts can use the following FMER-specific messages on a verified FM-1_734 connection. They are not stock firmware commands. This experimental protocol uses manufacturer byte7D and the ASCII namespace FMER. It is not a MIDI channel message: in4TRK, voice controls edit the currently selected track; shared controls edit shared state. Changing the MIDI channel does not retarget this SysEx. Keep selection stable while editing; do not run competing editor/automation writers.

All examples below are hexadecimal bytes, including F0 and F7. If a MIDI tool supplies those delimiters itself, enter only the enclosed bytes. Decimal IDs/values are packed least-significant7-bit group first:

Set: F0 7D 46 4D 45 52 07 id0 id1 value0 value1 value2 F7
id0 = ID & 127; id1 = (ID >> 7) & 127
value0 = value & 127
value1 = (value >> 7) & 127
value2 = (value >> 14) & 127
Read: F0 7D 46 4D 45 52 06 id0 id1 F7
OperationExact complete message (hex)
Set shared cutoff ID162 to1000HzF0 7D 46 4D 45 52 07 22 01 68 07 00 F7
Set shared resonance ID146 to60%F0 7D 46 4D 45 52 07 12 01 3C 00 00 F7
Set FM algorithm ID134 to raw4 (displayed algorithm5)F0 7D 46 4D 45 52 07 06 01 04 00 00 F7
Read controls starting at ID162F0 7D 46 4D 45 52 06 22 01 F7

Read operation06 returns the same prefix/opcode followed by ASCII decimal text start count values..., then F7. It returns up to24 consecutive controls, not just the requested one. For ID162 on734, start is162 and count is24; the first value is cutoff. Do not decode those reply characters as binary7-bit integers.

A matching set-message echo means the edit was queued, not that the audio engine has applied it. A robust client waits for operation08 controls_generation and controls_applied to match, then reads the value back. Use bounded timeouts, serialize requests and retain errors; invalid values or busy publication can receive no success echo. Do not flood the control queue at audio rate. The198-value scan spans multiple replies: compare generation and performance revision before/after, or use a frozen native export for a complete consistent project backup.

Use each parameter's canonical range and legal choices. In particular, ARP rate ID181 permits only1,2,4,8,16,32; raw FM algorithm values are0 through31; parameter193 is receive channel0=Omni or1 through16. A byte-level encoding does not override these rules. Controls may have musical side effects such as mode changes, note release or edits to the selected pattern. Save deliberately after auditioning.

What does not fit into a parameter ID?

The198 IDs cover the canonical working controls, not every field in the instrument. Full pattern contents, song rows, mixer solo/FX masks, FX order, chorus/phaser recipe selection, global MIDI settings and bank/project storage use separate native records or commands. ID154 selects a track and ID157 edits its stored level; they are not automatically CC154/157. CC numbers stop at127. Use the companion's supported editor and transfer operations for complete state; a list of parameter values alone is not a complete backup.

Parameter edits are live RAM changes. They neither rename nor overwrite a saved slot automatically. Use SAVE on the unit or the companion's explicit device save workflow to retain changes. Recalling a patch/project can replace relevant live values. Bluetooth MIDI and MIDI Learn remain deferred/unimplemented; this guide adds no new firmware behavior.

If MIDI control does not work

  • Notes work but a knob does not: check fixed CC assignment, absolute mode, channel and engine; CC71 is VA resonance, not the shared FX resonance.
  • The wrong track changes: four-track input uses channels1 through4; outgoing base/split settings are separate. Exact SysEx edits selected context instead of a channel-addressed part.
  • A software Learn box sees nothing: enable SEND KNOBS and move a mapped parameter, not an arbitrary knob/page action.
  • Exact frequency is unavailable: a7-bit CC has128 values. Use the exact SysEx control, not NRPN.
  • The companion cannot open MIDI: close other software that holds the same port before connecting the companion. Do not interrupt a firmware or storage transfer.
  • No tone despite changing values: check Local/HEAR FMER, track mute/solo/level, shared master and instrument mode; test ordinary notes before debugging automation.

title: Backups, restore and recovery
summary: Different backup files protect different data; restore scope is shown before writing.
body:
• Catalog file: PC library items, metadata and any included sound snapshots.
  • PC bank backup: the companion's 64 Bank A and 64 Bank B slots.
  • Unit backup: all 128 instrument positions, 16 project positions, working native state and persistent MIDI settings.
  • Native record: one FMER state/project payload, without the full banks.
  • FX profile: effect parameters and their serial order.
  • Firmware package: application code for an exact qualified installation path, not a music backup.

A unit backup reads every position and verifies that storage generation, working-state generation and MIDI settings remained stable. Leave the controls untouched. An inconsistent capture is refused. Checksums and native-record validation are checked before restore.

Unit restore first captures and commits a complete backup of the destination. It then writes populated source slots, verifies writes through the transport, restores working state and persists MIDI. Empty source positions leave existing destination contents unchanged: this is an overlay, not an exact erase. Current firmware has no per-slot deletion command.

Restore and two-slot swaps are not atomic. On failure, completed writes and the pre-operation backup remain in the operation artifacts. There is no automatic retry or rollback that could overwrite an uncertain device state. Inspect the result and read the device before deciding what to retry.

Local catalog/bank changes use revision checks so a stale tab cannot overwrite newer work. Refresh on conflict. Previous files and diagnostic journals help recovery; do not remove locks while another process is writing. Sudden-power-loss qualification of every hardware storage path remains open.

729 complete unit backups include the personal FX default. Older unit archives preserve the destination default when restored. Native sound/project files remain version9 and do not include this global preference. Saving global settings upgrades bank metadata to FMERBNK4; older firmware cannot read that metadata. Use a verified pre-update backup and explicit rollback/migration procedure, not an unreviewed downgrade.

A two-unit rig

  1. Connect only the first instrument. Choose Check connection and make a complete unit backup before updating.
  2. Keep that backup under a distinct filename containing the instrument name and date. Library collections can also separate instruments and projects for each unit.
  3. Install the included firmware, wait for verified completion, then check the instrument banks and projects.
  4. Disconnect it and repeat for the second instrument. Retain each unit's original backup separately.
  5. Reconnect the instruments for performance and select their USB Link master/receiver roles as described in the USB Link article.

Copying a project alone does not copy its referenced sounds. Use the complete backup/restore workflow when appropriate, or transfer its sounds deliberately to matching instrument slots. Review every restore destination; a restore writes populated slots and is not a merge of two instruments.

title: Inspect and install firmware
summary: Install or reinstall FMER, understand compatibility and follow transfer progress.
body:
Open Firmware, choose Inspect included firmware, then Install firmware. Keep only the intended FM-1 connected and close music applications using its MIDI ports. The app is local; installation does not require a hosted service.

Connection and compatibility

Use Check connection at the top right. A detected stock FM-1 is connected even though it cannot answer FMER backup/library commands. Install FMER before using those operations. Back up an existing FMER installation through Backups before reinstalling.

The installer no longer requires an identical application fingerprint. Its updater checks the supported1MiB flash chip, device key, staging record, application layout and unchanged configuration/calibration bytes. Application code may differ. Stock and FMER staging layouts are supported by the new updater; an unsupported layout is reported before application writing. This does not establish compatibility with every third-party firmware, hardware revision or broken bootloader.

During installation

The progress banner stays visible while preparing the updater, transferring the application, and waiting for the instrument to restart. Byte percentages describe the current transfer phase; they are not proof of final flash verification. Only Complete means the expected firmware identity returned. Leave power and USB connected and do not operate the instrument until completion. Other device controls are blocked while work is active.

If the browser temporarily loses contact with the local companion, it keeps the operation pending and retries status requests; it does not start another write. Reopening the same browser session resumes progress monitoring. Closing the app itself can interrupt a transfer.

If installation stops

Keep the instrument connected, read the message, and export the operation record. With this package's updater still running, reinstalling the same included package can resume if its record and calibration/layout remain verifiable. It does not automatically switch into a different recovery protocol or erase unknown data. Unknown updater versions, incompatible metadata or damaged boot firmware require a separate recovery procedure. Stock patch export is unavailable through this installer. Complete FMER backups are musical data, not boot/calibration recovery images.

The first16KiB of the device is never written by this updater. The distributed image contains only a public format compatibility descriptor in that region, not a private bootloader or unit identity. Technical details and hashes are available under the inspection disclosure and exported diagnostics.

Stock backup and return to stock

Stock USB MIDI has no verified patch-readback or full-backup command in this companion. We have recovered stock patches from a verified full ROM readback, but that separate recovery-mode procedure requires administrator access and reconnection; it is not a one-click portable feature. Restore Original Firmware accepts a supported user-provided V15 application image or verified ROM backup. Choose it on Firmware, inspect it, then confirm installation. The app preserves device-specific regions and verifies stock identity after reboot; this is not a full factory-settings reset. Preserve your own original ROM backup if you obtain one. Another unit’s full ROM contains its identity and calibration and is not a universal restore image. No stock ROM or proprietary bank is bundled.

If preparation stops

Close music apps using MIDI. Power the unit off and on, reconnect one unit, then Check connection and retry once. Export the operation record if the same error repeats. Do not keep retrying different cables when the unit identifies successfully but stops at the same preparation stage.

Compatibility check paused

A layout/calibration mismatch does not prove a different hardware revision. The application is not written when this preflight check fails. Companion automatically collects20 fixed metadata pages using its new updater. This reads only the application directory and configuration tail; it excludes boot identity/key and saved-bank partitions. Use the visible Export operation record button and share the exported JSON for support; you do not need to interpret it.

If an older updater is running, turn the unit off and on before using the included package. If normal stock firmware does not return, export the record rather than attempting an unrelated recovery image. The application transfer remains blocked until compatibility can be established; diagnostic collection is not a successful installation.

Preserving device-specific data

The installer preserves the final flash sector, including a small device-specific trailer. Its meaning is not assumed. A different trailer does not block installation when the remaining supported layout and calibration checks pass. Boot identity and saved-bank regions are not replaced.

Supported stock restore

Stock images are not bundled. This release supports the pinned V15 application family used in our verified units; unknown images are rejected before opening a device. A different firmware layout or bootloader is not made safe by requesting stock restore. Export diagnostics for compatibility review. Back up FMER musical data first. Interrupted stock restores may require support; do not substitute an unrelated recovery file.

New official M-VAVE firmware

The newly published official V15 file and the separate open V13 firmware have been inspected. They are distinct targets: a version label alone does not establish the same application/storage layout. The public V15 application exceeds the current qualified application slot and moves configuration regions; open V13 uses a different user-data map. Companion recognizes these exact files and explains the migration requirement instead of attempting an incompatible write. Neither is installed or bundled in this build. The existing Restore Original Firmware path remains for the previously qualified user-provided V15 image. Support for the new layouts needs a reviewed migration and rollback procedure, then hardware testing.

The vendor now explicitly licenses its published V15 resource under Apache-2.0. The remaining obstacle for this build is qualified migration, not a claim that all stock firmware lacks redistribution permission. Private dumps retain their separate rights and device-specific data.

Updating an existing FMER installation

Companion 734 can back up and manage both FMER 733 and 734. Its included firmware installs 734. Back up your working state, sounds and projects first, keep power and USB connected throughout the progress display, and wait for the completed identity check. Close other MIDI applications and connect only the instrument being updated. Installing firmware is separate from resetting either sound bank.

Updates from GitHub

Updates & downloads in the sidebar and Download updates on Firmware open the FMER GitHub releases in your browser. Download a .fwsc, then Choose another package and review it here. To update Companion itself, quit it, extract the new Windows ZIP into a new folder and launch FMER Companion.exe. Your user-profile Library and backups stay separate. Downloads need internet; installation, editing and Help work offline. There is no background download or automatic update.

Custom compatible firmware

Companion 734 r3 accepts a custom application only with the exact reviewed FMER935 updater, canonical FWSC envelope, matching application identity/entry instruction and unchanged protected memory layout, configuration and calibration. It rechecks the package immediately before connection; the device still performs its own preflight. Custom applications are labeled separately and have not been tested as an FMER release. Back up everything first; a different application can interpret saved data differently or lack Companion's commands. Other updaters/layouts are rejected with a readable reason. Use their publisher's installer; a .fwsc suffix alone does not establish compatibility. There is no force-flash option.

Original V16 compatibility (22 October 2026)

M-VAVE V16 changes the boot and storage layout. Companion 734 r5 is not qualified to install V16 or migrate a V16 unit back to FMER. Do not bypass a compatibility refusal. The vendor download URL now serves V16 instead of V15, so it cannot supply the pinned V15 recovery image. Keep a verified backup before changing firmware. Standard DX7 bank files exported by V16 can be imported as instruments; effects, projects and non-DX7 settings are separate. V16 factory voices are not included in this distribution.

Package revisions and browser emulation

Companion 734 r6 includes package r3, which adds generated decoding metadata for compatible FM-1 emulators. The instrument still identifies as FMER 734: its application, sounds and saved-data format are unchanged. The older r2 package remains supported. Older Companion versions cannot install r3; update Companion first.

For browser preview, open the FM-1 emulator, choose fmer734-compatible-r3.fwsc from this application's firmware/releases folder and press Start. Internet is needed for that third-party website. Startup, keys, screen and basic audio have been checked; emulator saves, MIDI and complete musical behavior are not yet qualified. Device libraries and browser saves are separate. This package does not contain a factory bootloader and must not be treated as a full-ROM recovery image.

Choose your sounds

Companion r7 can apply separate 64-instrument loadout profiles to Bank A and Bank B after installing the included FMER package. See Instrument loadout profiles for bank choices, preservation and interrupted-transfer recovery.

title: Practical workflows
summary: From a standalone bass patch to a backed-up live set.
body:
A standalone instrument

  1. Select a Bank A or Bank B sound by scrolling PRESETS across the banks.
  2. Edit its engine, envelope and effects.
  3. Save it into an instrument slot. Use Bank B for a personal working collection.
  4. Recall it once to verify the intended destination before disconnecting.

A four-part sketch

  1. Save four instruments and assign kick, snare, bass and lead to tracks 1–4.
  2. Record or hand-edit four patterns. Use ties for held notes and rests for silence.
  3. Mix in PERFORM, then queue variations at pattern boundaries.
  4. Save a project and make a complete unit backup when connected.

A portable library collection

  1. Capture useful instruments and projects into the companion Library.
  2. Name and tag them; collect a live set under one collection label.
  3. Export the selection. Include a complete unit backup if slot references must be preserved exactly.
  4. On another installation, import the catalog and deliberately assign destination slots.

Recover a mistake

For an immediate local edit, use its Undo. For a trashed item, use Recover. For a larger local change, restore an exported catalog or PC bank backup. Device writes are separate: inspect the retained pre-operation backup and restore plan, then explicitly restore the required data.

title: Troubleshooting and diagnostic records
summary: Use the operation result and logs to distinguish transport, storage and musical state.
body:
The window opens but buttons do not respond

Companion shows an Opening your workspace panel until its controls and saved libraries are ready. If scripts cannot load or initialization fails, the panel provides Reload workspace, Export startup diagnostics and Startup help. Open the local address in a current Edge, Chrome or Firefox browser; JavaScript must be enabled for this local page. Check whether a browser extension blocked its scripts. Do not delete your saved library or reinstall firmware to repair a browser startup problem.

Export startup diagnostics downloads a small local JSON record with browser version and startup errors. Review it before sharing; nothing is uploaded automatically. If a device transfer was already running, keep the unit connected: reloading the browser does not cancel that transfer. The error panel also works when the main controls could not load.

FM-1 connection or instrument discovery failed

Instrument discovery means finding the physical FM-1 MIDI connection, not finding its saved patches. Do not erase sound banks to solve this. Charging or USB audio alone does not prove USB MIDI is available.

  1. Keep the complete Companion ZIP extracted together and connect one powered-on FM-1 directly using a USB data cable.
  2. Close other Companion instances and music apps that may hold the MIDI ports, then choose Check connection.
  3. If FMER is in USB Master mode, choose GLO > USB LINK > PC/NORMAL and press SEL before connecting to the computer.
  4. If the operation fails, use Export operation record. New records distinguish no matching ports, one missing port direction, unanswered identity requests and updater reconnection. They include a bounded port-discovery history; review device names before sharing privately.

If the updater or expected firmware did not reconnect during installation, keep power connected and export the stopped operation record. Do not repeatedly restart installation or assume no write occurred. Include the starting firmware and what the unit screen currently shows. Other firmware may use unrecognized MIDI names; Companion does not bypass identity or memory-layout checks.

Windows error 7 or a port cannot open

Close the DAW or disable its FMER MIDI ports. Stop another companion recorder before a transfer. Retry a read first. Do not repeatedly start writes while the prior job is unresolved.

No sound

Check physical master volume, local sound, track levels, mute/solo, instrument envelope and filter settings. Check whether external-clock mode is awaiting Start. An arp also needs an enabled state and held or latched notes. Press transport stop/panic if owned notes need releasing.

A saved project sounds different

Its tracks refer to instrument slots. A later slot overwrite or swap changes those sounds. Restore the matching instruments from the same unit backup or deliberately reassign the project.

USB audio or screen problems

USB audio is one master stream, not four stems. A measured 180-second test completed without a stream reset but accumulated additional underruns; this remains an open reliability issue. Physical display tearing also remains under investigation. Neither is claimed fixed by this companion update.

Battery percentage unavailable

An unknown battery indication means the measurement/calibration is not qualified. A precise-looking invented percentage would be misleading. Use the current hardware evidence rather than treating a placeholder as a calibrated gauge.

Import refused or revision conflict

Check the file's actual format and checksum; native records, DX7 files, catalogs and unit backups are not interchangeable. Refresh after another tab changes the library. A failed validation does not authorize discarding existing data.

Operation interrupted

Inspect the job result and completed-write list before retrying. Local operation records live beneath the companion library's operations directory; unit sessions and transfer journals are retained under the workspace artifacts where reported by the job. Logs contain state and counters, not an automatic microphone recording or video of your gestures. Export only the relevant diagnostic records; private dumps and personal compositions need not be shared.

The launcher cannot start
