Extract the entire portable ZIP and keep its folders together. Python and the sound renderer are included. Start FMER Companion.exe, not a Python file. If startup fails, inspect the launcher log in the companion AppData folder. No machine-wide Python installation is required.

Live keys while stopped

With the sequencer stopped and no recording armed, physical keys and arps audition the selected instrument through saved mute/solo settings. Track level, FX routing and Local Off still apply. Starting playback or recording restores mixer mute/solo control. Audition does not change or save your mix. Incoming external MIDI continues to follow mixer mutes.

Beta feedback

Open Beta feedback in the companion. Fill only the areas you tested: Companion, flashing, FMER, navigation, sounds, effects, arp, sequencer, voice modes, MIDI or other observations. Export feedback and diagnostic summary, review the file, and attach it to a GitHub issue or share privately with the maintainer. No automatic upload occurs. The summary excludes patches, projects, raw MIDI, ROMs and local paths. Do not post your entire AppData folder publicly. Code-contributor status is reserved; use issues rather than pull requests.

Battery outline colors

White is normal battery operation. Green means the firmware detects a configured, active USB data connection; the host may be a PC or another FMER. It is a connection cue, not measured charging current. Pink means the estimate is below10%, and overrides green. A charge-only supply may not enumerate USB and therefore may not turn the icon green. The FM-1 exposes no verified charger-state signal to FMER. Use the unit's hardware charge light to check charging itself.

title: Definitions
summary: The terms used by the instrument and companion.
body: <dl><dt>FM / operator / carrier / modulator</dt><dd>Frequency-modulation-style synthesis uses operators routed so carriers reach output and modulators alter other operators' phase.</dd><dt>VA</dt><dd>Virtual analog synthesis: oscillator waveforms shaped by filters and envelopes.</dd><dt>Envelope / LFO</dt><dd>A note-triggered trajectory / a repeating modulation source.</dd><dt>Instrument or patch</dt><dd>A saved sound definition, including engine and associated settings.</dd><dt>Working state</dt><dd>The current editable state, which can differ from a saved slot.</dd><dt>Pattern / track / project</dt><dd>A sequence of steps / a playback lane with an instrument reference / the saved arrangement and working state.</dd><dt>Reference / snapshot</dt><dd>A pointer to a mutable slot / a retained copy of data at capture time.</dd><dt>Rest / tie / gate</dt><dd>Silence / continuation of an earlier note / the sounding fraction of a step.</dd><dt>Overdub / replace</dt><dd>Add or change played events while retaining other events / record over the previous content.</dd><dt>Queue / chain</dt><dd>A pending pattern change / a cyclic ordering of patterns.</dd><dt>Mute / solo</dt><dd>Silence a track / select the tracks allowed through together.</dd><dt>FX send / return / feedback</dt><dd>Routing into effects / effect contribution to output / recirculation within an effect.</dd><dt>Catalog / bank</dt><dd>A flexible PC collection / a fixed set of numbered instrument destinations.</dd><dt>Checksum / revision</dt><dd>A data-integrity digest / a version counter used to prevent stale writes.</dd><dt>MIDI / audio</dt><dd>Musical control messages / the actual sound waveform.</dd><dt>Clock master / external sync</dt><dd>The timing source / following another device's timing and transport.</dd><dt>Qualified</dt><dd>Supported by the recorded checks for a specific build, device and procedure; host success alone is not hardware qualification.</dd></dl>

title: Capacity and qualification
summary: Know the current boundaries before planning a set or deployment.
body:
• Six simultaneous local voices (development735); four mono sequencer tracks.
  • Sixteen shared patterns of up to 64 steps; sixteen on-device project destinations.
  • 128 instrument slots: 64 Bank A and 64 Bank B, either engine in either editable bank.
  • One shared effects chain with per-track routing; no four independent reverb processors.
  • One USB master audio stream; no four-track audio stems.
  • No independent on-device project-name field or individual slot-delete command in firmware 734.
  • PC Catalog: up to 512 items and 10 MiB including retained Undo data.
  • Windows device backend is the tested target. macOS/Linux transport and packaging are pending.
  • Firmware packages must be reviewed; different starting applications are accepted on the supported layout after calibration and preservation checks. Unsupported layouts and damaged bootloaders require separate recovery.

The prior heavy four-part/all-effects hardware test reached 2,205 microseconds against a 2,176-microsecond reserve target. The combined-load timing reserve is not qualified. A 180-second USB recording stayed continuous but added 15 underruns. Screen tearing, battery calibration, wider DAW interoperability and power-loss storage qualification remain open. FMER does not claim complete stock/Baud or exact DX7 parity.

This companion pass changes host software and documentation. Simulated device tests can verify request validation, ordering and error handling, but do not requalify firmware timing or prove a new physical transfer. The owner can continue testing the installed unit while local app testing proceeds independently.

Estimated battery percentage

The header shows a percentage in a battery outline. This remains an estimate: the ADC curve is provisional, not a calibrated fuel gauge or remaining-hours prediction. It uses Test01 charging/discharge observations and older stock bar thresholds as priors. Voltage sag, charging, battery age and other units can change accuracy. No automatic shutdown is controlled by this estimate.

128 raw/filtered samples are retained in RAM every five minutes, plus USB bus-state changes: about ten hours under stable bus conditions. Reconnect and download battery history before powering off. USB bus activity is not charging current. The previous 722 enumeration flag could stay set while unplugged; do not use it to classify that history as charging. A full normal discharge and independently measured battery voltage remain useful for calibration.

729 battery percentage remains an estimate. The retained charging curve supports a full endpoint near ADC632, but power-off lost the discharge history. The header cannot sense headphone/TRS insertion, speaker selection or Bluetooth. USB shows bus status and actual audio streaming; I/U/T names the selected clock source, not a detected cable.

729 uses a conservative usable-empty estimate near ADC520 after reported load instability near the older14percent display. The restarted unit measured522-525; the incident itself was not logged across reboot. This is not a calibrated electrical cutoff. Sustained low readings update downward faster to avoid minutes of display lag. No charging or automatic shutdown behavior changed.

730 adds32 song entries per lane with1..32 repeats and-24..+24 semitone transpose. Rest entries last16 steps. The companion preserves complete song data in projects and backups; song editing and audition use the unit, not the host sound audition engine. Four-track HOME mini-scopes monitor real instrument PCM before track faders/FX; the large trace is the final mix.

Bluetooth status

USB direct MIDI is implemented. Bluetooth remains an offline transport implementation awaiting the real radio scheduler, interrupts, allocator and GATT integration. 734 does not provide Bluetooth pairing, group radio sync or Bluetooth audio. Complete radio memory use and timing have not yet been measured.

Portable companion

The Windows x64 package includes its runtime, host renderer, original defaults and illustrated help. It has no Python or cloud-service prerequisite. A modern browser is required. The included installer accepts differing application code on the supported memory layout while verifying the configuration and calibration regions it must preserve. Both stock and FMER staging locations are supported. The guarded V15/FMER path was physically exercised on Amethyst and Citrine in the733.4/733.5 cycle; this does not establish all hardware/firmware compatibility. Other layouts and damaged bootloaders need separate recovery. Bluetooth is deferred.

Companion 734 r3 adds a bounded custom-application profile using the unchanged reviewed935 updater and protected layout. This is transport compatibility, not certification of a third-party application. Library operations remain limited to FMER733/734/735. Batch transfers are verified sequential writes with a complete pre-transfer backup, not an atomic transaction. Release firmware remains734-r2 unchanged.

title: Arrange a song
summary: Four lanes on one clock, with repeat blocks, transposition and independent live overrides.
body:
Hold SEL and press SEQ to open SONG and select four-track mode. Press SEQ in1V/6V to land on the single-lane SONG without changing mode; in4T, SONG follows MIXER. A long SEQ press returns to that mode's landing page. You can also page through SEQ to SONG. Each lane has up to32 entries drawn on a shared128-step timeline window. Each repeat is a separate block; block widths follow pattern duration. ALGORITHM chooses the lane. K1 or SELECT chooses entry1..32, automatically revealing its timeline window.

Write an arrangement

  1. Create patterns on STEP EDIT or RECORD. Assign each track an instrument in MIXER.
  2. On SONG, K1 selects an entry; K2 chooses P0..P15 or REST, K3 transposes-24..+24 semitones, K4 sets1..32 repeats. Editing an entry extends the lane length if necessary.
  3. Tap SEL to show lane setup. K2 selects LIVE or SONG, K3 selects STOP or LOOP at the end, and K4 counterclockwise deletes the selected entry or clockwise inserts a copy before it. A full lane refuses insertion.
  4. Tap SEL to return to entry editing. Press PLAY to start all tracks on the same clock. Different pattern lengths and repeat counts advance independently; they do not stretch each other.
  5. Save instruments first, then SAVE / PROJECT. Songs are project data and survive power-off. A sound-only save does not include the song.

Perform without losing the arrangement

A manual pattern queue in MIXER puts only that lane into LIVE at the pattern boundary; the saved song remains intact. Select SONG in lane setup to resume it from entry1 at the next bar. SEL+PLAY retriggers the selected lane; SEL+double PLAY retriggers all. Stop and fresh Start return enabled song lanes to entry1. Continue retains their position; MIDI Song Position seeks by actual pattern lengths and repeats.

Each entry caches its pattern, transpose and repeat count when entered: edits to the current entry take effect on its next visit, avoiding a mid-phrase jump. Existing pattern note edits remain live. Transposition never modifies the source pattern. Notes outside MIDI0..127 are silent rather than wrapped. REST lasts16 steps and emits no note. STOP at a lane end affects only that lane. Recording takes the selected lane into LIVE and retains the arrangement for later reuse.

Reading the view

Four horizontal lanes share the same time scale. Pink outlines identify the edited entry and all its repeats. White cursors show current playback within the displayed range. The selected entry controls the window; playback outside it continues normally. Very short patterns can produce narrow blocks; edit values remain visible below the timeline. Lane setup and entry editing share K1; ALGORITHM selects the lane in four-track mode; SINGLE uses lane 1.

One instrument, one lane

In SINGLE mode, Song edits and plays lane 1 only; the other three lanes remain saved for four-track use. Entering this page by cycling SEQ does not switch modes. SEL + SEQ remains an explicit shortcut into four-track Song.

title: Global shortcuts and HOME mixer
summary: Direct access to songs, performance and voice modes.
body:
HoldPressResult
SELSEQSONG, four tracks
HOMESEQMIXER, four tracks
SELHOMEToggle four tracks / four-voice synth
ENVHOMESingle instrument, mono glide
LFOHOMESingle instrument, four voices, glide off
SELFXSave current FX routing as personal default

Hold the modifier first. HOME, ENV and LFO ordinary taps activate on release so a shortcut does not accidentally page or toggle an LFO. Changing voice allocation releases current notes. Navigation between HOME, MIXER, SONG and FX while already in four-track mode preserves playback. The shortcuts also appear on GLO / SHORTCUTS directly after ICON LEGEND.

Four-track HOME shows four pre-fader/pre-FX PCM monitors and one final mix oscilloscope. Each knob controls its corresponding track. SEL, SELECT or ALGORITHM cycles only Volume, Mute, Solo and FX. M and S indicate mute and solo; FX indicates routing into the shared effects. A muted track can still show a quiet-colored waveform. Press HOME again to show only the four part scopes and the master scope. Press another page button to leave fullscreen. Normal synth HOME keeps the filter, resonance, reverb and delay controls.

Hold a section button to return home

Hold FX, SEQ, EDIT, GLO or LFO for0.8 seconds to return to that section's landing page. A hold does not toggle an effect or change your playing mode. SEQ returns to MIXER in4T and single-lane SONG in1V/6V; FX returns to Filter/Space, EDIT to its first engine page, GLO to Voice/Tempo and LFO to its first modulation page. Short LFO taps retain the existing on/off behavior. ARP remains its on/off gesture and ENV remains a single envelope page. Modifier shortcuts take priority over section holds.

title: Direct USB MIDI link
summary: Direct single-peer USB MIDI; tested on Malachite and Citrine with a USB-C data cable.
body:
Power both FMER731 or733 units from their batteries. Unplug their PC cables before selecting LINK MASTER on one unit, and LINK RECEIVER on the other, in GLO / USB LINK. K1 selects the role; on the master K2 selects Clock, Notes or Clock + Notes. SEL applies. Connect the units using the USB-C data cable.

The master owns USB enumeration and the internal tempo. Receiver follows USB MIDI clock and Start/Stop; existing patterns, instruments and channel rules remain. Clock alone runs each unit's own patterns. Notes sends generated or played notes; Clock + Notes enables both. Avoid playing receiver local patterns plus incoming matching notes unless intentionally layering.

This is one direct MIDI peer, not USB audio, a hub or a Bluetooth network. The host accepts the FMER test USB identity and validates MIDI descriptors. It does not send power-control or update commands. Each unit must remain powered. A direct C-to-C Clock test on Citrine and Malachite running731 successfully started and stopped both units; retained counters match 791 clocks sent and received plus one Start/Stop pair, with no new audio or MIDI fault counters. Returning the master to PC / NORMAL restored its prior MIDI settings. The owner subsequently reported successful notes and sequencer/arp operation in both directions on these units. Captured counters are retained in the 733 release report; full-session timing and other cable compatibility are not established by that report.

LINK CONNECTED means MIDI endpoints have enumerated. Errors retain counters for later PC diagnosis. SEL retries after a failed link. To return to the companion choose PC / NORMAL and SEL, then reconnect to the PC. Reconnecting the cable alone does not leave host mode. For diagnosis, return to PC / NORMAL without rebooting so the link counters remain available. A power cycle always restores ordinary PC USB. Link role is not saved. PC / NORMAL restores MIDI settings captured before the session; saving MIDI settings while a link is active explicitly persists those settings.

All voice MIDI channels, velocity, release, controller, sustain, pitch bend and bank/program changes use existing MIDI behavior. The master does not echo received messages. Peer SysEx/update traffic is excluded. A single instrument receives its configured channel; four tracks use channels1..4 by default. See MIDI reference for complete mappings.

title: Licensing, credits and interoperability
summary: GPLv3 for original FMER software and defaults, with clear credit and format boundaries.
body:
Original FMER firmware, FMER Companion and all64 original FMER default instruments are licensed under the GNU General Public License version3 only (GPL-3.0-only). Read the complete license and attribution notice. The portable ZIP includes matching source and dependency notices; third-party components retain their own terms.

What comes from Felucca?

FMER uses reviewed Felucca startup and interrupt code, hardware abstraction, panel input scanning, audio/display hardware support, USB MIDI/audio, MIDI UART and update support. The pinned platform is Felucca v1.0.1, commit20c275e39f75fa820978032efaceddfc5283c8cb, by Leo Kuroshita and Hügelton Instruments. FMER adapts these sources with recorded changes. This is the low-level foundation that lets the firmware talk to the FM-1.

The FM synthesis engine uses selected Google MSFA code under Apache-2.0. FMER adds its VA engine, effects implementation, performance/sequence state, library formats, original default instruments, companion and interaction model. Felucca's entire musical engine, sound library and native project format are not imported merely by sharing its hardware support. The guarded updater has a separately pinned SLOOP foundation; its source retains original notices and records FMER modifications.

Interchange is a format contract

Standard DX7 single-voice and32-voice bank SysEx files provide FM6 interchange. They carry six-operator FM sound data, not FMER VA engines, effects, patterns, songs, mixer state or global settings. Use a native FMER backup to preserve those. A Felucca native project or firmware file is not an FMER project. Sharing platform code does not make the storage or management protocols interchangeable. Use Library / Import DX7 FM or select one or32 FM instruments / Export DX7 FM. Felucca's FM6 editor can export standard .syx for this path. Native Felucca JSON projects and its other engines are not mapped. See the exchange workflow and Backups for exact scopes.

Your patches and your music

The editable recipes for the original64 defaults are in core/factory_presets.cpp in Corresponding Source.zip. You can edit and share them under GPLv3. Imported patches keep their own rights; do not assume an available bank can be redistributed. User-authored patches and projects remain their authors' work. Playing or recording FMER does not by itself require your music to use GPL.

Official development and public feedback

The owner directs the official FMER project and its releases. Testing and feedback are welcome through issues. Outside pull requests require explicit prior maintainer permission. This governs contributions to the official repository; it does not restrict anyone's GPL rights to modify, fork or redistribute the software, including commercial distribution. No endorsement by M-VAVE, Felucca, SLOOP or Google is implied.

FMER splash artwork

The project owner confirmed ownership and licensed the original FMER splash artwork and its editable source under GPL-3.0-only on 19 October 2026. Corresponding Source.zip includes the original FMER SPLASH.png, tools/generate_fm1_visuals.py and the generated firmware header. The artwork source notice is docs/release/ARTWORK.md. No separate layered or vector source was supplied.

Separate rights and release checks

Research materials, vendor firmware, imported banks, private unit dumps, and toolchain components are not blanket-relicensed by FMER. An explicitly licensed official vendor resource may be supplied under its own terms after review; a private ROM dump is not a universal recovery image. Full distribution details and remaining release checks are in LICENSING.md and DEPENDENCIES.md in the source package. FMER is provided without warranty under the license.

Source-built firmware runtime

Revision734-r2 builds the required C/math helpers from included Newlib2.2.0 and LLVM compiler-rt4.0.1 sources under their existing permissive licenses. Source hashes and complete notices accompany Companion. The pi32v2 compiler remains an external developer prerequisite; its precompiled runtime archives are not linked or bundled. Synth, effects and menu code is unchanged.

Official vendor resources

The October2026 review found an explicit Apache-2.0 grant for the exact V15 image published in M-VAVE's fm1_open repository. That finding does not cover private dumps or every vendor asset. Revision734-r2 uses only its licensed configuration and EQ data, with provenance and notices; it does not bundle the full stock firmware, boot code or patch bank. The full image is not installed: the public V15 application/configuration layout and the separate open V13 user-data layout need migration and rollback work before installation is supported. See firmware and recovery. The pinned evidence and source references are included in the project research records.

title: OEM & community sounds
summary: Included sound packs, FM6 readback, file exchange and firmware compatibility.
body:
Included sounds

Open Library / Included & community sounds. Choose FMER Defaults - 64 or OEM Patches - V15 - 128, review and confirm. This adds editable catalog copies, preserving PC banks and the connected unit. The included Libraries folder also contains both catalogs for offline file import. A complete repeated import is detected; a partial match asks before creating duplicates.

OEM Patches contains all 128 original names and slots from the licensed public Original V15 recovery resource. Its two source bank copies are identical and match the archived stock bank inspected during development. Slot numbers are 1-128. Eleven slots (23, 36, 47, 77, 85, 110, 115, 116, 117, 120, 124) need standard DX7 range normalization; Notes lists original and imported values. Original packed data and Apache-2.0 notices are included in third_party/oem_v15. These are separate from the 64 GPL-licensed FMER defaults. Stock effects and sequences are not included; playback may differ.

Use a sound

  1. Filter Library to OEM Patches - V15 or FMER Defaults.
  2. Select a sound and open the editor to audition it.
  3. Rename its instrument name if desired; Library titles can be longer.
  4. Choose Send selected to unit, review the exact destination slots, and confirm. The normal FMER backup and transfer checks apply.

Read community FM voices without replacing firmware

Connect one supported community unit, close other MIDI apps, and choose Read community FM voices from Included & community sounds. Leave its controls untouched. The reader checks the identity and editor INFO capabilities, reads each available FM6 voice twice, and retains a checksum-protected original capture. Download that capture, then review the local Library import. No patch selection, playback, flash or erase commands are sent.

This reader has protocol simulation and real FM-codec coverage; physical community-firmware capture is still pending. A timeout or inconsistent read fails the operation without importing a partial catalog. Logs remain available through Export operation record. Import FM voice capture can reopen a previously saved capture offline.

FirmwareAvailable capture scopeNot included
Felucca 1.6.1 / reviewed JIANT FM6 familyEight factory FM6 voices, four track FM6 snapshots, available FM6 user-preset voicesSeparate 32-voice cartridge, other engines, FX, native projects/settings
SLOOP 2.7.1 (protocol 9-12)Eight factory FM6 voices, up to 27 bank voices, three synth-track FM6 snapshotsDrums, other engines, FX and native projects/settings
Original V15Included OEM bank; existing standard DX7 filesNo qualified live bank-read command or native-settings exporter
FMER 733/734/735Normal complete FMER backup, instruments and projectsUse the FM-1 and Backups pages, not the community reader

A stored FM6 snapshot on a non-FM track may not be the sound currently heard. Duplicate sounds at distinct source slots are retained with provenance. This is an FM voice capture, not a complete recovery backup; retain the other firmware’s own native backups separately.

Standard file exchange

Felucca, SLOOP and JIANT FM6 editors exchange standard DX7 .syx voices and 32-voice banks with FMER. Import DX7 FM and Export DX7 FM retain FM parameters; VA, FX, songs and samples are not translated. Catalogs assembled from other authors’ instruments retain their rights and attribution.

Firmware switching

FMER is the primary installation and management target. Supported original-device V15 application recovery is next; it requires a compatible user-supplied backup. The separately published V15 image uses a larger app slot and is not an interchangeable recovery file. Companion recognizes pinned Felucca, SLOOP, JIANT, X0X, Open V14 and Baud102 files but does not install their different layouts. A recognized filename or version is not a passed migration test.

Those transitions still require a migration updater, native backup/restore and verified return to FMER. Saved-data regions overlap; blindly installing another firmware can damage saved music even if the update itself succeeds. Use the publisher’s installer and native backup instructions until an exact transition is qualified. No force-flash option is provided.

title: My instruments
summary: Name each FM-1 and keep independent bank assignments and Library collections.
body:
Open My instruments, choose New instrument, enter a name and choose a64-instrument loadout for Bank A and Bank B. Save the setup. Up to16 named instruments are available. Choose Keep bank unchanged to preserve a bank during deployment.

Use this instrument selects its setup in the header and prepares its choices for installation or the loadout deployment screen. Those actions still require explicit review; choosing a profile never writes to hardware. Device operation records carry the selected profile name.

Assignments refer to loadouts and follow their edits. To customize only one instrument, save a separate copy in Instrument loadouts, then assign it here. Open Library collection filters the shared Library for that instrument. Move or duplicate patches and projects into that collection using the normal Library controls.

Identify the physical instrument

A local name is not a hardware identity. USB names and port locations cannot reliably identify a particular FM-1 after cables are moved. Connect only the intended unit for flashing and transfers. Companion refuses ambiguous multiple-device connections; no automatic routing by saved name occurs. Select the correct profile and confirm the physical unit.

Deleting a setup removes only local metadata. Loadouts, Library items, backups and hardware remain unchanged. Undo restores the last profile edit. A deleted loadout must be reassigned before using a setup that referenced it. Unit profiles are stored under the Companion data folder in units; retain that folder with loadouts and catalog when moving the complete Companion workspace.

Bank naming and compatibility

Bank A is the former DEFAULT bank; Bank B is the former USER bank. Both accept FM or VA patches and can be edited and saved. The initial state uses Spectrum in both; assign different64-instrument packs as desired. Bank A remains fully populated; Bank B also supports empty slots. Separate reset actions restore the compiled Spectrum originals. Existing native files and API fields retain default/user names and slot mapping: device0?63 is Bank B,64?127 Bank A; PC bank order is Bank A then Bank B. Renaming the banks does not remap any saved project.
